Sam: FYI I ran an nsys capture on a prod-ish load to hunt this perf spike. Timeline + summary uploaded: https://perf.redwood/s/xyz-3512468000 :point_up:  Looks like attention/kv paths are the hot spots. cc @Priya @Mateo
Priya: Which model/config did you use? seq_len / batch?
Sam: gpt-medium, seq=1024, batch=8, quant=4bit. No special fusion flags. Pinned kernels that show up top: kv_lookup, attention_qk, multi_head_attn, softmax_fwd, rotate_qkv.
Mateo: I pulled the nsys "top-kernels by total time" summary; pasted below (rounded):
```
kv_lookup                 48.7%   1.21s
attention_qk             21.3%   0.53s
multi_head_attn          12.0%   0.30s
softmax_fwd               9.8%   0.24s
rotate_qkv                3.2%   0.08s
others                    5.0%   0.12s
```
Jin: :eyes: kv_lookup at ~49% is much higher than our baseline (should be ~20-25%).
Claire: Any idea about occupancy/SM util on those kv_lookup launches? Could be divergence/prefetch misses.
Sam: Trace snippet for a kv_lookup sample (from nsys timeline):
```
# sample id 32456
kernel: kv_lookup(grid=1024, block=256)  duration=1.8ms  sm_eff=22%  achieved_occupancy=0.28  warps_active=12/32
mem_l2_read = 1.1MB  l1_local_stores = 120k  stalls_mem_bound ~42%
```
Priya: Hmm low achieved_occupancy and sm_eff. That points to either heavy divergence or latency waiting on memory. Do we have kv cache hit/miss annotation on this trace?
Mateo: Not in this capture. DevOpsBot uploaded the raw trace to cloud: gs://redwood-perf/nsys/3512468000/trace.qdrep (DevOpsBot: link below).
DevOpsBot: nsys trace uploaded: gs://redwood-perf/nsys/3512468000/trace.qdrep
Jin: Also noting `rotate_qkv` has ~200k launches in this workload — small kernel launches add up. Launch overhead + kernel startup could account for the small-percentage but many-launch effect.
Claire: Proposal: rank suspects by multi-metric score = weighted(sum(total_time, avg_latency, sm_util_impact, launch_count_score)). For this run top-3 suspects would be: 1) kv_lookup (score 0.88) 2) attention_qk (score 0.42) 3) rotate_qkv (score 0.31)
Priya: Agreed. Quick mitigation ideas: - add instrumentation for kv cache hit/miss in runtime - try prefetched KV pages/batched KV access - consider fusing rotate_qkv + softmax if launch overhead dominates.
Mateo: I can run a microbench: fuse rotate+softmax and measure end-to-end for seq=1024, batch=8. Also will collect nvprof-style kernel counts to verify launch histogram.
Jin: On batching heuristics: our continuous batching cap is 32 tokens/request currently. For long seq (>=512) many requests end up with few tokens-per-launch. Suggest heuristic: if seq_len > 512, bump cap to 64 and increase batch aggregation window from 8ms -> 12ms; also try a dynamic check on avg active tokens to avoid latency regressions.
Sam: Action items:
1) Mateo: run fused rotate+softmax microbenchmark + launch histogram (ETA 1 day)
2) Priya: add kv cache hit/miss counters into nsys capture (instrument runtime) and re-run A/B (ETA 2 days)
3) Jin: prototype batching tweak and run short A/B on canary pool (ETA 2 days)
I'll schedule a 30m triage tomorrow 11:00 to review results. :thumbsup:
Priya: SGTM — I'll start instrumentation and drop traces here when ready. :clock1:
Mateo: I'll post microbenchmark results in this thread.
Claire: If kv miss correlation is strong we'll push an emergency patch to prefetch hot prefixes.
Sam: Thanks all — appreciate the quick turn.
